subject: Discovery recap & bake-off next steps with Acme Health
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Bryan Liu <bryan.liu@acmehealth.com>, Dana Park <dana.park@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap & bake-off next steps with Acme Health

Thanks for taking the time today — appreciated the context on Acme Health's inference priorities. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so everyone has the same expectations.

Pain points you shared
- Latency spikes on peak business hours (p95 up to 1.6s for short prompts) impacting user experience.
- High per-token cost from current cloud endpoints when serving at scale.
- Need for deterministic behavior across model variants for clinical response safety checks.

Current stack
- Inference: TGI-hosted endpoints + managed cloud GPUs for peak batch jobs
- Data: internal S3 with PII redaction layer, sample eval sets stored in their data lake
- Requirements: SOC2 + enterprise VPC for PHI-sensitive workloads

Success criteria for bake-off (proposed)
- Latency: p50 < 120ms and p95 < 350ms for 512-token generation on 8k context workload
- Throughput: sustained 200 qps for 1k concurrent users with <500ms median latency
- Cost: per-1k-token unit cost that reduces current spend by >= 35% (target range provided below)
- Quality: answer-level accuracy on the provided sample_eval_set >= current baseline (we'll use your annotated labels)
- Reliability: failure rate <0.1% over 2-hour sustained run

Benchmark comparison scope
- vLLM self-hosted baseline (your current preferred open-source stack)
- TGI-managed endpoints (what you currently run in prod)
- Redwood inference variants (quantized and standard profiles) across hosted/dedicated modes

Attachments
- acme_bakeoff_acceptance_criteria.xlsx (acceptance matrix + initial targets)

Next steps / ask of Acme Health
1) Confirm the benchmark targets above (latency/throughput/cost/quality) or tell us which numbers to adjust.
2) Share a small (~1k prompt) sample_eval_set CSV and an example production request payload (headers, tokens) so our harness is aligned.
3) Approve a 90-min kickoff for a hands-on bake-off where our SE (Rishi) will run the harness. We propose Wednesday 7/22 or Thursday 7/23 morning PT.
4) Provide an ephemeral credentials (short-lived S3 or staging endpoints) or allow us to run against a sanitized copy of your sample data.

If that all looks good, Rishi will share the exact harness, required IAM permissions, and a proposed timeline for the bake-off.

Thanks — I’ll wait for a quick confirm on targets and preferred kickoff slot.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0137

--
Attachment: acme_bakeoff_acceptance_criteria.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Bryan Liu <bryan.liu@acmehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dana Park <dana.park@acmehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 17:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap & bake-off next steps with Acme Health

Thanks Marissa — solid recap, thanks for pulling that together. A few clarifications from our side: 

- The latency/throughput targets look reasonable as starting points. We likely need p95 < 300ms for the most latency-sensitive flows, but we can be flexible for background jobs.
- For quality, we'll run the acceptance tests against our labeled clinical QA set (I'll share a sanitized subset).
- For cost, please include both token-based cost and an estimate for reserved/dedicated capacity (we're evaluating committed monthly spend vs pay-as-you-go).

Requests: 
1) Can you confirm the exact model variants/endpoints you'll test for "Redwood inference variants" (names + quantization profile)? We want to line up comparables (vLLM/TGI).
2) We'll share sample_eval_set.csv by EOD Wednesday. We'll also need the test harness and instructions so our infra team can review the network/S3 access requirements.

Roadblocks: We have an internal security questionnaire related to ephemeral credentials and data retention. Can you confirm Redwood's default retention for logs during a bake-off and if we can opt-out of storing raw prompts?

We're good to do the 90-min kickoff — preferred slot is Thu 7/23 9:00am PT.

Thanks,
Bryan
Director of Data Platform
Acme Health
Bryan.Liu@acmehealth.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Bryan Liu <bryan.liu@acmehealth.com>, Dana Park <dana.park@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap & bake-off next steps with Acme Health

Hi Bryan / Dana — looping in the SE plan and what we'll need from Acme to run an apples-to-apples bake-off.

High-level plan
- Run three baseline configurations: (1) vLLM on your self-hosted A100 nodes (your baseline), (2) TGI-managed endpoints (your current prod), (3) Redwood-hosted + dedicated (quantized 4-bit and FP16 profiles).
- Metrics: end-to-end latency (p50/p95/p99), sustained throughput (qps), token-cost (USD/1k tokens), and answer-level F1 on your labeled eval set.
- Methodology: run 30m warm-up, then 2 x 1-hour sustained runs at target qps levels (50%, 100% of expected peak). We'll measure tail latency under background load to simulate spikes.

Data & infra ask
- Sample eval set: please provide the CSV and a schema (we got Marissa's note you'll share ~1k prompts).
- Access: short-lived S3 credentials or a presigned bucket we can pull from; we do not need write access unless you want logs back.
- Security: Redwood will not persist raw prompts by default; logs are retained for 7 days for debugging and can be turned off for the bake-off on request. We can also run in-dataplane-only mode if needed for PHI-sensitive flows.

Deliverables
- redwood_bakeoff_plan.pdf (step-by-step harness + exact model config tables)
- sample_eval_set.csv (empty template attached)
- link to test harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/bakeoff-harness (instructions in the PDF)

Schedule
- Proposed kickoff: Thu 2026-07-23 09:00-10:30 PT — Rishi (SE) + Marissa (AE) + Bryan/Dana + your infra lead.

If that works, Marissa can confirm and we'll send a calendar invite + pre-bake-off checklist.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai

--
Attachments: redwood_bakeoff_plan.pdf, sample_eval_set.csv
